title: 保温杯为什么能保温
title_en: How a Flask Keeps Your Tea Hot
summary_zh: 早上倒进去的热茶，下午还烫嘴。保温杯靠的是两层杯壁之间的真空，还有亮亮的内壁和盖子。读完你能用被动语态和 so… that… 解释一个日常物品的原理。
body: If you pour hot tea into a good flask in the morning, it can still be hot in the afternoon. This is not magic. A flask is designed to stop heat from escaping, and it does this in three clever ways. Heat usually moves from hot things to cold things. It can travel through solid materials, it can be carried by air, and it can also spread out as light that we cannot see. Most flasks have two walls, one inside the other, with a thin space between them. The air is taken out of this space, so it becomes a vacuum. Without air, heat cannot be carried across the gap, and very little gets through to the outside. The inside walls are often shiny, which helps to reflect some of the heat back into the drink. Finally, the lid is very important, because a lot of heat would escape from the top if it were open. The same flask also keeps cold drinks cold, since it stops outside heat from getting in. Some flasks work so well that you need to be careful with very hot drinks. So next time you take a sip of warm tea, remember the empty space that is doing the work.

questions.prompt: What does the text mainly explain?
options: How a flask keeps drinks hot or cold
questions.evidence: A flask is designed to stop heat from escaping, and it does this in three clever ways.

questions.prompt: Why can a flask also keep cold drinks cold?
options: It has ice inside the walls
It stops heat from the outside getting in
Cold drinks do not need a lid
The shiny walls make the drink colder
questions.evidence: since it stops outside heat from getting in

questions.prompt: What is a "vacuum" in "it becomes a vacuum"?
options: a space with almost no air in it
questions.evidence: The air is taken out of this space, so it becomes a vacuum.

questions.prompt: What do the shiny inside walls do?
options: Reflect some heat back into the drink
questions.evidence: which helps to reflect some of the heat back into the drink

vocabulary.example: I always take a flask of coffee to work.
Close the window to stop the heat escaping.
There is a vacuum between the two walls.
White walls reflect light and make a room look bigger.
She took a sip of her hot chocolate.

expressions.note: 科普文常用来引出原理。
stop sth from doing sth 阻止……做……
Very little light gets through to the bottom of the sea.
so + 形容词/副词 + that 引出结果。
Take a sip of water before you speak.

knowledge.quote: The air is taken out of this space, so it becomes a vacuum.
knowledge.explanation: 被动语态 is taken out：重点是“空气被抽走”，不需要说是谁做的。说明物品原理时很常用。

knowledge.quote: The inside walls are often shiny, which helps to reflect some of the heat back into the drink.
knowledge.explanation: which 指代前面整件事（内壁是亮的），补充说明它的作用。

knowledge.quote: Some flasks work so well that you need to be careful with very hot drinks.
knowledge.explanation: so… that… 引导结果状语从句：保温效果太好，所以要小心烫。

speaking: 用 1 分钟给朋友解释：保温杯为什么能保温？用上 stop… from… 和 so… that…。
writing: 用 80–100 词解释一个你每天用的物品是怎么工作的（如雨伞、冰箱贴、保温杯）。用一个被动句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 … work(s) so well that … 写一句话，夸一个好用的东西。
task.model: Some flasks work so well that you need to be careful with very hot drinks.
